Mayoral Car Hire

By: Harri Vithi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A small town mayor racking up the kilometers while tax payers foot the bill

Unique Selling Point:
It's a story of abuse of power told through the odometer.

Summary:
Mayor Mamikie Maditswako Theresia Mokoena of Nketoana Municipality (since 2016) is under investigation for spending R33,932 for fuel and R64,893 for a rented vehicle between May and June of this year she reportedly travelled 6943km between 18th of May and 18 of June in a rented Toyota Fortuner.


Further information:
Background

The little known municipality of Nketoana in the Free State has a total area of 5611k㎡ is quite small you would agree.
Population: over 60 000.

The municipality has faced consistent mismanagement, questionable tender
practices and unapproved expenditure going as far back as the previous mayor Mandla
Mlaba, former CFO of Nketoana municipality Vincent Mkhefa and service provider

Caroline Nketu accused of tender corruption for a project to facilitate the installation of
playground equipment at the municipality parks. As a result the municipality lost
R364,000 paid to Nketu for work not done, Mkhefu made payments of R165,000
R198,500 on two separate occasions to Nketoana who in turn made payments to Mlaba
of R100k each the trio was arrested in 2019.
https://www.corruptionwatch.org.za/eight-years-for-errant-cfo-with-series-of-local-govt-
related-graft-charges/

The AG’s report over the last 4 years does not sing praises either. According to the
auditor general reports the municipality declared R480 million in irregular expenditure for
the 2022/2023 financial year and R421 million for the 2021/2022 financial year R15.8
million was incurred in contravention of supply chain management requirements, in
2021/2022 R56 million was spent. There was R980 million in unauthorized expenditure in
2022/2023 up from R811 million in 2921/2022 the municipality suffered a net loss of
R170 million ending 30/06/23 and it’s liabilities exceeded its assets by R740 million there
was also R47.6 million in fruitless and wasteful expenditure.
https://mfma-2023.agsareports.co.za/municipality/2-nketoana


This following 2 accidents where the mayors cars owned by the municipality were written off.

In August 2021 MTM’s BMW four series was involved in an accident she appears to have rented a car until August 2023 when a new Haval H9 was bought, R850,000 was spent during this period on car hire and by November 2023 the Haval was a write off and the mayor was renting once again first a Ford Everest and then a Fortuner. Odometer readings for May to June are also confusing with some readings having less mileage than previous visits to the fuel stations additionally the mayor seemed to spend the entire month in Gauteng

https://www.thesouthafrican.com/news/politics/nketoana-municipality-mayor-mamiki-
mokoena-rented-car-and-fuel/


2. Far from being the first time this controversial mayor has popped up in the headlines,
in 2018 just 2 years after her election as mayor reports of a toxic work environment
surfaced and allegations against the mayor by municipality employee Mangaliso
Hlongisane who opened a case of assault stating that the mayor had slapped and
punched him following a labor dispute Mangaliso claimed that his work as a community
activist raising service delivery issues earned him a transfer to the water and sanitation
department where he was expected to collect and empty buckets of human waste as the
town still used bucket toilets he refused the move and was backed by his union but was
apparently told by the mayor the week before the transfer that she would fix him.

https://www.sowetanlive.co.za/sundayworld/news/2018-07-10-small-town-mayor-with-
violent-streak/

3. In 2022 the EFF opened criminal charges against MTM accusing her of stealing from
the public purse the community also claimed it had been writing to the MEC, Cogta HOD
and the Premier about the municipality not following IDP processes and were not getting
any joy from any of the departments.
https://sundayworld.co.za/news/fed-up-community-wants-corrupt-mayor-council-speaker-
fired/

4. Bringing us to 2024 in February the municipality failed to pay employees salaries on
time and according to the DA in the province some have not received a full salary, in July
the manager of expenditure Maremela Moksatala claims he was headbutted by CFO
Jabulani Makubu after he refused to implement payment for a colleagues car allowance
who did not qualify. Maremela alleged that after he refused to implement payments
because internal protocols were not followed and that the municipality was under the
scrutiny by the national treasury. Jabulani Makubu attacked him in his office, which he
denies the financial implications would be R9,981.23 per month and R119,775.10 per
year. It appears there may be a trend in lack of enforcement in transport policy!

https://www.sowetanlive.co.za/news/south-africa/2024-07-29-cfo-head-butted-me-for-car-
allowance-manager/

5. In August the embattled municipality was in the headlines again this time for failing
to penalise a contractor linked to the mayors cousin for poor performance. The contractor
failed to meet the deadline for completion of a concrete Reservoir project in February of
this year the contractor Little Rocky and Baleleri baAfrica were appointed to construct the
Reservoir worth more than R17 million. Sources alleged the Director of Baleleri baAfrica
Thapelo Nakedi was mayor MTM’s cousin and his mother is an employee of the
municipality R1,824,360 was paid but the project was still sitting at 10%.
The contractor shot back that he had an accumulated invoice submitted in January of R900,000 which remains unpaid after SARS attached the municipalities account after failure to pay
R2,622,867 and at the same time Rudnat Projects CC obtained a court ordered to attach
R5,130,032 For outstanding payments.


With management like this it’s no wonder it is referred to as a one horse town,
development is slow and benefits only trickle from those in power to those favoured,
complaints going back years and no action taken. Will this be the straw that broke the
camel's back.

Summary: Mayor Mamikie Maditswako Theresia Mokoena of Nketoana Municipality (since 2016) is under investigation for spending R33,932 for fuel and R64,893 for a rented vehicle between May and June of this year she reportedly travelled 6943km between 18th of May and 18 of June in a rented Toyota Fortuner. Further information: Background The little known municipality of Nketoana in the Free State has a total area of 5611k㎡ is quite small you would agree. Population: over 60 000. The municipality has faced consistent mismanagement, questionable tender practices and unapproved expenditure going as far back as the previous mayor Mandla Mlaba, former CFO of Nketoana municipality Vincent Mkhefa and service provider Caroline Nketu accused of tender corruption for a project to facilitate the installation of playground equipment at the municipality parks. As a result the municipality lost R364,000 paid to Nketu for work not done, Mkhefu made payments of R165,000 R198,500 on two separate occasions to Nketoana who in turn made payments to Mlaba of R100k each the trio was arrested in 2019. https://www.corruptionwatch.org.za/eight-years-for-errant-cfo-with-series-of-local-govt- related-graft-charges/ The AG’s report over the last 4 years does not sing praises either. According to the auditor general reports the municipality declared R480 million in irregular expenditure for the 2022/2023 financial year and R421 million for the 2021/2022 financial year R15.8 million was incurred in contravention of supply chain management requirements, in 2021/2022 R56 million was spent. There was R980 million in unauthorized expenditure in 2022/2023 up from R811 million in 2921/2022 the municipality suffered a net loss of R170 million ending 30/06/23 and it’s liabilities exceeded its assets by R740 million there was also R47.6 million in fruitless and wasteful expenditure. https://mfma-2023.agsareports.co.za/municipality/2-nketoana This following 2 accidents where the mayors cars owned by the municipality were written off. In August 2021 MTM’s BMW four series was involved in an accident she appears to have rented a car until August 2023 when a new Haval H9 was bought, R850,000 was spent during this period on car hire and by November 2023 the Haval was a write off and the mayor was renting once again first a Ford Everest and then a Fortuner. Odometer readings for May to June are also confusing with some readings having less mileage than previous visits to the fuel stations additionally the mayor seemed to spend the entire month in Gauteng https://www.thesouthafrican.com/news/politics/nketoana-municipality-mayor-mamiki- mokoena-rented-car-and-fuel/ 2. Far from being the first time this controversial mayor has popped up in the headlines, in 2018 just 2 years after her election as mayor reports of a toxic work environment surfaced and allegations against the mayor by municipality employee Mangaliso Hlongisane who opened a case of assault stating that the mayor had slapped and punched him following a labor dispute Mangaliso claimed that his work as a community activist raising service delivery issues earned him a transfer to the water and sanitation department where he was expected to collect and empty buckets of human waste as the town still used bucket toilets he refused the move and was backed by his union but was apparently told by the mayor the week before the transfer that she would fix him. https://www.sowetanlive.co.za/sundayworld/news/2018-07-10-small-town-mayor-with- violent-streak/ 3. In 2022 the EFF opened criminal charges against MTM accusing her of stealing from the public purse the community also claimed it had been writing to the MEC, Cogta HOD and the Premier about the municipality not following IDP processes and were not getting any joy from any of the departments. https://sundayworld.co.za/news/fed-up-community-wants-corrupt-mayor-council-speaker- fired/ 4. Bringing us to 2024 in February the municipality failed to pay employees salaries on time and according to the DA in the province some have not received a full salary, in July the manager of expenditure Maremela Moksatala claims he was headbutted by CFO Jabulani Makubu after he refused to implement payment for a colleagues car allowance who did not qualify. Maremela alleged that after he refused to implement payments because internal protocols were not followed and that the municipality was under the scrutiny by the national treasury. Jabulani Makubu attacked him in his office, which he denies the financial implications would be R9,981.23 per month and R119,775.10 per year. It appears there may be a trend in lack of enforcement in transport policy! https://www.sowetanlive.co.za/news/south-africa/2024-07-29-cfo-head-butted-me-for-car- allowance-manager/ 5. In August the embattled municipality was in the headlines again this time for failing to penalise a contractor linked to the mayors cousin for poor performance. The contractor failed to meet the deadline for completion of a concrete Reservoir project in February of this year the contractor Little Rocky and Baleleri baAfrica were appointed to construct the Reservoir worth more than R17 million. Sources alleged the Director of Baleleri baAfrica Thapelo Nakedi was mayor MTM’s cousin and his mother is an employee of the municipality R1,824,360 was paid but the project was still sitting at 10%. The contractor shot back that he had an accumulated invoice submitted in January of R900,000 which remains unpaid after SARS attached the municipalities account after failure to pay R2,622,867 and at the same time Rudnat Projects CC obtained a court ordered to attach R5,130,032 For outstanding payments. With management like this it’s no wonder it is referred to as a one horse town, development is slow and benefits only trickle from those in power to those favoured, complaints going back years and no action taken. Will this be the straw that broke the camel's back. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A small town mayor racking up the kilometers while tax payers foot the bill
metadata.Unique Selling Point: It's a story of abuse of power told through the odometer.
metadata.Summary: Mayor Mamikie Maditswako Theresia Mokoena of Nketoana Municipality (since 2016) is under investigation for spending R33,932 for fuel and R64,893 for a rented vehicle between May and June of this year she reportedly travelled 6943km between 18th of May and 18 of June in a rented Toyota Fortuner.
metadata.Further information: Background The little known municipality of Nketoana in the Free State has a total area of 5611k㎡ is quite small you would agree. Population: over 60 000. The municipality has faced consistent mismanagement, questionable tender practices and unapproved expenditure going as far back as the previous mayor Mandla Mlaba, former CFO of Nketoana municipality Vincent Mkhefa and service provider Caroline Nketu accused of tender corruption for a project to facilitate the installation of playground equipment at the municipality parks. As a result the municipality lost R364,000 paid to Nketu for work not done, Mkhefu made payments of R165,000 R198,500 on two separate occasions to Nketoana who in turn made payments to Mlaba of R100k each the trio was arrested in 2019. https://www.corruptionwatch.org.za/eight-years-for-errant-cfo-with-series-of-local-govt- related-graft-charges/ The AG’s report over the last 4 years does not sing praises either. According to the auditor general reports the municipality declared R480 million in irregular expenditure for the 2022/2023 financial year and R421 million for the 2021/2022 financial year R15.8 million was incurred in contravention of supply chain management requirements, in 2021/2022 R56 million was spent. There was R980 million in unauthorized expenditure in 2022/2023 up from R811 million in 2921/2022 the municipality suffered a net loss of R170 million ending 30/06/23 and it’s liabilities exceeded its assets by R740 million there was also R47.6 million in fruitless and wasteful expenditure. https://mfma-2023.agsareports.co.za/municipality/2-nketoana This following 2 accidents where the mayors cars owned by the municipality were written off. In August 2021 MTM’s BMW four series was involved in an accident she appears to have rented a car until August 2023 when a new Haval H9 was bought, R850,000 was spent during this period on car hire and by November 2023 the Haval was a write off and the mayor was renting once again first a Ford Everest and then a Fortuner. Odometer readings for May to June are also confusing with some readings having less mileage than previous visits to the fuel stations additionally the mayor seemed to spend the entire month in Gauteng https://www.thesouthafrican.com/news/politics/nketoana-municipality-mayor-mamiki- mokoena-rented-car-and-fuel/ 2. Far from being the first time this controversial mayor has popped up in the headlines, in 2018 just 2 years after her election as mayor reports of a toxic work environment surfaced and allegations against the mayor by municipality employee Mangaliso Hlongisane who opened a case of assault stating that the mayor had slapped and punched him following a labor dispute Mangaliso claimed that his work as a community activist raising service delivery issues earned him a transfer to the water and sanitation department where he was expected to collect and empty buckets of human waste as the town still used bucket toilets he refused the move and was backed by his union but was apparently told by the mayor the week before the transfer that she would fix him. https://www.sowetanlive.co.za/sundayworld/news/2018-07-10-small-town-mayor-with- violent-streak/ 3. In 2022 the EFF opened criminal charges against MTM accusing her of stealing from the public purse the community also claimed it had been writing to the MEC, Cogta HOD and the Premier about the municipality not following IDP processes and were not getting any joy from any of the departments. https://sundayworld.co.za/news/fed-up-community-wants-corrupt-mayor-council-speaker- fired/ 4. Bringing us to 2024 in February the municipality failed to pay employees salaries on time and according to the DA in the province some have not received a full salary, in July the manager of expenditure Maremela Moksatala claims he was headbutted by CFO Jabulani Makubu after he refused to implement payment for a colleagues car allowance who did not qualify. Maremela alleged that after he refused to implement payments because internal protocols were not followed and that the municipality was under the scrutiny by the national treasury. Jabulani Makubu attacked him in his office, which he denies the financial implications would be R9,981.23 per month and R119,775.10 per year. It appears there may be a trend in lack of enforcement in transport policy! https://www.sowetanlive.co.za/news/south-africa/2024-07-29-cfo-head-butted-me-for-car- allowance-manager/ 5. In August the embattled municipality was in the headlines again this time for failing to penalise a contractor linked to the mayors cousin for poor performance. The contractor failed to meet the deadline for completion of a concrete Reservoir project in February of this year the contractor Little Rocky and Baleleri baAfrica were appointed to construct the Reservoir worth more than R17 million. Sources alleged the Director of Baleleri baAfrica Thapelo Nakedi was mayor MTM’s cousin and his mother is an employee of the municipality R1,824,360 was paid but the project was still sitting at 10%. The contractor shot back that he had an accumulated invoice submitted in January of R900,000 which remains unpaid after SARS attached the municipalities account after failure to pay R2,622,867 and at the same time Rudnat Projects CC obtained a court ordered to attach R5,130,032 For outstanding payments. With management like this it’s no wonder it is referred to as a one horse town, development is slow and benefits only trickle from those in power to those favoured, complaints going back years and no action taken. Will this be the straw that broke the camel's back.
